name: molvic
author: shops-money-swapping
description:
molvic v3 (direction: shops, money and swapping) - THE SHOP SHELVES AND THE GOODS THAT GO
BACK WHERE THEY BELONG. PRIVATE; never shown to players.

WHAT v3 IS: A RE-SKIN OF v2. THE RULE, THE COUNTS, THE PLANTS, THE FOOTHOLD AND THE WITNESS
PROFILE ARE UNCHANGED - only the drawing changed. On 2000 seeds v3's picture is a pure relabelling
of v2's: same slot grid, same strays, same gaps, same n (0 structural mismatches). The judge scored
v2 kid 2.67: "a grid of capital letters between | and +---+ is a data table, not a drawing of a
shop shelf; a kid would say 'rows of letters where one letter repeats a lot', not 'oh, a shop!';
comparing two dense letter grids character by character is a chore." That is a salience problem
(DESIGN_LOOP lever 9), and garrow v4 fixed the same one by changing glyphs and the caption without
touching the rule. See challenges/lab/NOTES_shops.md (2026-09-05, v3).

CLUE = THE SHELF UNIT DRAWN FROM THE FRONT, plus one caption line "<n> home".
  A shop-front line carrying the fixed sign "THE CORNER SHOP" (identical in every clue, so it
  carries nothing), then 4 shelves. Each shelf is one row, LABELLED AT ITS LEFT EDGE with the name
  of its goods in capitals ("JAM  |", "EGG  |", "COD  |" - every name is three letters), then
  9-11 slots of 3 characters separated by a space, then "|"; a shelf edge "     +---...---+"
  is drawn under each shelf. A slot holds a good, drawn as the LOWERCASE 3-LETTER NAME of its kind
  ("jam", "egg", "cod"), or an EMPTY SLOT drawn "___". Every shelf's own goods match its label, so
  A SHELF BELONGS TO THE KIND WRITTEN ON IT - nothing has to be inferred from a majority (the
  majority still wins by >= 2 on every row, so the two readings never disagree).
  A STRAY is a good standing on somebody else's shelf: 5-8 of them, at most 3 on a shelf, never
  two of the same kind on one shelf. ONE OR TWO SHELVES ARE FULL (drawn solid, not one "___" on
  them); every other shelf has 2-3 gaps. Clue 393-465 chars, 9 lines + caption.
  The 21 kinds are three-letter shop goods: ale bun cod dip egg fig gum ham jam keg log mop nut
  pie rye soy tea urn veg wax yam (one per letter, so the first letter still identifies the kind).

ANSWER = THE CLUE'S PICTURE WITH THOSE n GOODS PUT AWAY. Exactly 2n slots change: each mover's old
slot becomes "___" and the first "___" on its own shelf becomes its shelf's goods. Nothing else
changes - the sign, the labels and the shelf edges are copied through. The answer is UNIQUE per
clue. The trailing "<n> home" line may be kept or dropped; both score 1 (house rule 2026-09-05).
Trailing spaces and trailing newlines are ignored.

RULE (one breath): TWO GOODS THAT STAND IN LINE - the same slot, one above the other - AND ARE
EACH ON THE OTHER'S SHELF BOTH GO HOME, AND A GOOD GOES HOME INTO THE FIRST EMPTY SLOT ON ITS OWN
SHELF; IF ITS OWN SHELF IS FULL THERE IS NOWHERE TO PUT IT, SO IT STAYS WHERE IT IS. Formally: a
good of kind H[k] at (row i, slot j) moves iff the good at (row k, slot j) is of kind H[i] AND
row k contains a gap; it is erased from (i,j) and written into the first gap of row k (the gap
positions are read off the CLUE, before anything moves). n counts the goods that move, so the two
pictures differ in exactly 2n slots. generate() never lets two movers want the same shelf.

WHAT THE RE-SKIN CHANGES, AND WHY EACH BIT
  (1) THE HOME SHELF IS WRITTEN, NOT COUNTED. "JAM  |" at the left edge says whose shelf it is, so
      "it goes home" is a place a kid can point at instead of a majority to be tallied. The scorer
      now reads the label instead of taking a majority - cheaper (496/512 chars) and it cannot be
      broken by a tie under hash randomisation.
  (2) GOODS ARE WORDS, NOT CAPITALS. "jam jam ___ egg jam" instead of "J J   E J". A stray now
      reads as a different WORD in a row of identical words; the eye finds it without counting
      columns, and lowercase goods against a capital label make the label unmistakably a label.
  (3) THE GAP IS A THING YOU CAN POINT AT. An empty slot is "___", not a blank. "The FIRST empty
      slot on its own shelf" is now a visible object with a position, which is exactly the half of
      the rule that a player has to buy with a demo.
  (4) FULL IS LOUD. A full shelf is a solid run of one word with no "___" anywhere in it; the
      refused good standing above it is visibly standing over a shelf with nowhere to go.
  (5) FLAVOUR THAT CARRIES NOTHING. The fixed sign "THE CORNER SHOP" sits in the top edge of the
      unit. It is byte-identical in every clue apart from its width, so it can carry no information;
      it is there so the first two seconds of looking end in "that's a shop".

OFFLINE CHECKSUM TEST (1200 clues; what fraction of clues each COUNT hypothesis reproduces)
  in-line mutual goods with room at home (TRUE)                          100.0 %
  in-line mutual pairs                                                    31.9 %
  in-line mutual pairs with room for both                                 11.2 %
  in-line mutual goods, room ignored (v1's rule, the players' reading)      0.0 %
  mutual goods, alignment ignored / strays in line / strays with room       0.0 %
An exhaustive search over conjunctions of nine natural per-stray predicates finds only two rules
that reproduce the caption everywhere: the true one, and its TWIN "in line, mutual, and the shelf
it is STANDING on is not full" - which per pair always counts the same but picks the other good
of the pair, and cannot be drawn (it would send a good to a full shelf). The twin is
indistinguishable from the caption alone and is settled by one look at a demo (12.3 % either way).

EVERY DEMO TEACHES THE WHOLE RULE. generate() plants, in every instance (audited, 4000 clues):
  P1  an in-line mutual good whose own shelf is FULL, so it stays        100 %
  P2  a mutual pair that is NOT in line, so neither moves                100 %
  P3  a third stray standing in a going-home column, whose own shelf HAS
      room -> kills "anything in line with a stray goes home"            100 %
  P4  a stray standing on a FULL shelf with room at home, that stays
      -> kills "the goods on the packed shelf get put away"              100 %
  P5  a stray with a GAP in line on its own shelf -> kills "it goes back
      if there is a space for it right there"                            100 %
  P6  every mover's home shelf has 2-3 gaps, and in every clue at least
      one mover's landing gap is neither the nearest gap to its column
      nor the nearest gap on its left -> "the FIRST gap" is forced       100 %
  P7  the movers are never simply the first n strays in reading order    100 %
  P8  for n >= 2, some movers climb and some are lifted down             100 %
  P9  every mover's landing gap is drawn "___" in the clue, so both ends
      of every edit are visible before the answer is drawn               100 %
  Configurations (4 shelves, F = full): n=0 [F=a,b; pair (a,b)]; n=1 [F=a; (a,b)] or
  [F=a,b; (a,b),(a,c)]; n=2 [F=a,b; (a,c),(b,d)]; n=3 [F=a; (a,b),(c,d)].

THE FOOTHOLD (lever 7). 12-12.5 % of clues say "0 home": nothing moves and the correct answer IS the
clue returned unchanged, caption kept or dropped. Those clues look exactly like the others - they
still carry an in-line mutual pair (both of whose shelves are full), a mutual pair out of line,
strays in line - so a demo-less player who reads "a shop shelf unit, things on the wrong shelf,
2 home" and echoes the picture scores ~12 %, and so does every count-based guess. What the clue
alone reveals about the answer's SHAPE: it is this same shelf picture with a few goods put away,
and the caption says how many go - so a demo-less player always has a well-formed attempt.

WITNESS TABLE (1500 fresh clues, shipped scorer; identical to v2 row by row. Templates render with
the TRUE drawing convention - a player who has seen a demo and holds the wrong rule - unless BLIND):
  BLIND: in-line mutual pairs swapped in place (v1's rule + v1's edit)     0.0 %
  BLIND: the same, only the pairs with room, swapped in place            12.3 %
  BLIND: in-line mutual goods rubbed out                                  0.0 %
  BLIND: tidy up - every stray put right where it stands                  0.0 %
  clue returned unchanged                                                12.3 %  <- the foothold
  clue unchanged, caption dropped                                        12.3 %
  only the good on the LOWER shelf of each pair goes home                20.7 %  <- the top rival
  only the good on the UPPER shelf of each pair goes home                19.9 %
  n strays at random go home                                             16.5 %
  every in-line mutual good goes home (fullness ignored)                  0.0 %
  the whole pair goes home if either of the two has room                 12.3 %
  TWIN rule (the good on a shelf that has room), moved / swapped          12.3 % each
  true movers -> the LAST gap / the nearest gap / the nearest gap left    12.3 % each
  true movers -> the first gap on the shelf they were standing on        12.3 %
  true movers, old slot filled by the partner (swap AND move)            12.3 %
  true movers, old slot filled by the shelf's goods                      12.3 %
  true movers copied home, old slot left as it was                       12.3 %
  true movers rubbed out, never arriving                                 12.3 %
  true movers, and the refused goods vanish too                           0.0 %
  a good needs a gap IN LINE at home                                     12.3 %
  any stray with a gap on its own shelf goes home                         0.0 %
  any stray in line with another stray goes home                          0.0 %
  any mutual stray (alignment ignored) goes home                          0.0 %
  any stray on a FULL shelf with room at home goes home                   0.0 %
  the first n strays in reading order / the strays on the fullest shelf  12.3 / 6.4 %
  one fixed real answer for every clue / demo replay                      0.0 %
  TRUE RULE (solve), caption kept / dropped / rows padded               100.0 %
No template beats 21 %. The two that pay are the pair-half guesses (which of the two goods in a
one-sided pair moves), and they are a coin flip only on the n=1 clues; one demo settles them.

WELL-FORMEDNESS (14 attacks x 1500 clues, all 0.0 %): gaps drawn as dots, lowercased (the labels
go), shelf edges removed, slot spacing squeezed out, rows reversed, caption count changed, the
answer sent twice, a junk line appended, half the picture, the caption alone, the empty string,
4000 chars of junk, one fixed answer, another clue's answer. Declared leniencies: trailing
newlines, trailing whitespace on any row, caption present or absent. The scorer rebuilds the whole
expected picture from the clue and compares line by line, so nothing about the rule can be
smuggled through the form. Uniqueness: 747 270 single-character mutations and 64 400 single-slot
mutations (every slot swapped for every other kind and for a gap) of true answers, 0 scored 1.

ENGINEERING (4000 fresh seeds). generate mean 0.45 ms, median 0.27, p99 4.7, max 8.8 (v2 measured
back to back on the same box: 0.44 / 0.26 / 4.6 / 9.0 - the re-skin costs nothing), 0 fallback
uses, 2000/2000 clues distinct and deterministic (byte-identical output under four
PYTHONHASHSEEDs); solve 0.019 ms; score 0.015 ms on real answers and on 4000-char junk. Scorer
496/512 chars, solve 1266/5000, generate 8.5k/50000, clue and solution 393-465/1024. n is
0 (12.5 %), 1 (16 %), 2 (22 %) or 3 (49 %). An independent re-implementation (tokens by regex, the
shelf's kind by MAJORITY rather than by its label, picture rendered from scratch) agreed with
solve/score on 1200/1200 clues, and the label agreed with the majority on every row of all of
them.

INTENDED SPLIT. With a demo: the pictures differ in 2n slots that come in pairs - a word gone from
one shelf and a "___" filled in on another - so "it has been put away on its own shelf" is the
first thing a player sees; which gap is forced by P6, and the good that DIDN'T move (P1) is
standing over a shelf drawn solid. Without a demo: the caption says goods go home, so the natural
reading is "the two in each other's places trade back" - which is v1's rule with v1's edit, and it
scores 0.0 %; the honest blind attempt is to echo the picture, which pays 12 %. The residual risk
is a theorist who both finds the count rule offline (it needs two conjuncts, one of which - "there
is room at home" - only makes sense once you believe the good MOVES) and then buys the landing
convention with live probes; durnel v2 carries the same risk and held at 10 % blind.

LEVERS. Too easy: (a) require the caption dropped (removes the identity foothold and the offline
checksum); (b) let a shelf be full on one side only (a good goes to the first gap AFTER its own
column); (c) draw the goods with a price so the row is wider and the eye has more to skip.
Too hard: (a) drop the full-shelf clause, so every in-line mutual good goes home (measured: the
caption is then reproduced by the pair count, which is most of the way back to v1);
(b) draw one good already put away in the clue as a worked instance; (c) always give a mover's
shelf exactly one gap, so "the first gap" is "the gap".
generate:
# THE SHOP SHELVES AND THE GOODS THAT GO BACK WHERE THEY BELONG.
# 4 labelled shelf rows of slots; the label says what the shelf is for. A STRAY is a good
# standing on somebody else's shelf. Caption "<n> home": n goods go home. Two goods that stand
# IN LINE (the same slot, one above the other) and are EACH ON THE OTHER'S SHELF both go home,
# and a good goes home into the FIRST EMPTY SLOT (___) on its own shelf, leaving its old slot
# empty. A FULL shelf (no empty slot at all) has no room, so a good whose shelf is full stays.
# Every clue plants: a good with no room at home, so it stays (kills "all the in-line pairs");
# a mutual pair NOT in line; a third stray in a going-home column whose own shelf HAS room;
# a stray on a full shelf that has room at home; a stray with a gap in line on its own shelf.
AL = "ABCDEFGHJKLMNPRSTUVWY"
NM = dict(zip(AL, "ale bun cod dip egg fig gum ham jam keg log mop nut pie rye"
                  " soy tea urn veg wax yam".split()))
NM[" "] = "___"
BR = "     +" + "-" * 39 + "+"
FB = ("     +=========== THE CORNER SHOP ===========+\n"
      "BUN  |___ bun bun bun dip ___ bun bun mop ___|\n" + BR + "\n"
      "MOP  |bun mop mop nut mop mop mop mop mop mop|\n" + BR + "\n"
      "NUT  |nut ___ ___ mop bun ___ nut nut nut nut|\n" + BR + "\n"
      "DIP  |dip dip dip dip bun dip dip dip dip dip|\n" + BR + "\n2 home")


def generate(seed):
    r = random.Random(seed)
    zero = r.random() < 0.12                     # decided once, before any retry
    for _ in range(500):
        W = r.randint(9, 11)                     # slots per shelf
        LT = r.sample(AL, 4)                     # what each shelf is for
        a, b, c, d = r.sample(range(4), 4)
        if zero:                                 # the only in-line pair is refused by two
            FUL, AM = [a, b], [(a, b)]           # full shelves, so nothing moves at all
        else:
            FUL, AM = r.choice([([a], [(a, b)]),                    # n=1
                                ([a, b], [(a, b), (a, c)]),        # n=1
                                ([a, b], [(a, c), (b, d)]),        # n=2
                                ([a, b], [(a, c), (b, d)]),
                                ([a, b], [(a, c), (b, d)]),
                                ([a, b], [(a, c), (b, d)]),
                                ([a], [(a, b), (c, d)]),           # n=3
                                ([a], [(a, b), (c, d)]),
                                ([a], [(a, b), (c, d)]),
                                ([a], [(a, b), (c, d)])])
        G = [[LT[i]] * W for i in range(4)]
        occ = [set() for _ in range(4)]

        def put(host, home, j):                  # a good of LT[home] left on shelf `host`
            G[host][j] = LT[home]
            occ[host].add(j)

        def free(*rows):
            return [j for j in range(W) if all(j not in occ[i] for i in rows)]

        def kinds(i):
            return [G[i][x] for x in occ[i]]

        ok = True
        cols = []
        for p, q in AM:                          # the in-line pairs: each on the other's shelf
            f = free(p, q)
            if not f:
                ok = False
                break
            j = r.choice(f)
            put(p, q, j)
            put(q, p, j)
            cols.append((j, p, q))
        if not ok:
            continue
        pm = [(p, q) for p in FUL for q in range(4)                 # plant: a mutual pair NOT in
              if q not in FUL and (p, q) not in AM and (q, p) not in AM]   # line - and the good
        r.shuffle(pm)                            # left on the full shelf DOES have room at home
        for p, q in pm[:1]:
            f1 = [x for x in free(p) if LT[q] not in kinds(p)]
            f2 = [x for x in free(q) if LT[p] not in kinds(q)]
            if not f1 or len(f2) < 2:
                ok = False
                break
            j1 = r.choice(f1)
            f2 = [x for x in f2 if x != j1]
            if not f2:
                ok = False
                break
            put(p, q, j1)
            put(q, p, r.choice(f2))
        if not ok or not pm or not cols:
            continue
        j, p, q = r.choice(cols)                 # plant: a third stray in a going-home column,
        opt = [(m, e) for m in range(4) if m not in (p, q) and j in free(m)   # standing there
               for e in range(4) if e != m and e not in FUL                   # with room at
               and G[e][j] != LT[m] and LT[e] not in kinds(m)]                # home, and staying
        if not opt:
            continue
        opt.sort(key=lambda t: (t[0] not in FUL, r.random()))
        m, e = opt[0]
        put(m, e, j)
        if r.random() < .5:                      # a lone stray for texture, standing pat
            lone = [(i, e, x) for i in range(4) for e in range(4) if e != i
                    for x in free(i) if G[e][x] != LT[i] and LT[e] not in kinds(i)]
            if lone:
                i, e, x = r.choice(lone)
                put(i, e, x)
        if max(len(o) for o in occ) > 3 or not 5 <= sum(len(o) for o in occ) <= 8:
            continue
        NF = [i for i in range(4) if i not in FUL]
        gap = {i: set() for i in NF}
        cand = [(k, x) for k in NF for x in range(W) if x not in occ[k]
                for i in range(4) if i != k and x in occ[i] and G[i][x] == LT[k]]
        if not cand:                             # plant: a stray with a gap in line on its own
            continue                             # shelf (there is room, but not in line)
        k, x = r.choice(cand)
        gap[k].add(x)
        for k in NF:
            f = [x for x in range(W) if x not in occ[k] and x not in gap[k]]
            need = r.randint(2, 3) - len(gap[k])
            if len(f) < need:
                ok = False
                break
            gap[k] |= set(r.sample(f, need))
        if not ok:
            continue
        for k in NF:
            for x in gap[k]:
                G[k][x] = " "
        st = [(i, x, LT.index(G[i][x])) for i in range(4) for x in sorted(occ[i])]
        mov = [(i, x, k) for i, x, k in st if G[k][x] == LT[i] and " " in G[k]]
        n = len(mov)
        if len({k for i, x, k in mov}) != n:      # two goods must never want the same gap
            continue
        if not [1 for i, x, k in st if G[k][x] == LT[i] and " " not in G[k]]:
            continue                             # plant: a good with no room at home, so it stays
        if not [1 for i, x, k in st if i in FUL and " " in G[k] and (i, x, k) not in mov]:
            continue                             # plant: a stray on a full shelf that has room
        if not [1 for i, x, k in st if (i, x, k) not in mov and " " in G[k]
                and any(m != i and G[m][x] not in (" ", LT[m]) for m in range(4))]:
            continue                             # plant: in line with a stray, room at home, stays
        gp = {i: [x for x in range(W) if G[i][x] == " "] for i in range(4)}
        if n and not [1 for i, x, k in mov
                      if gp[k][0] != min(gp[k], key=lambda y: abs(y - x))]:
            continue                             # the first gap is not the nearest gap
        if n and not [1 for i, x, k in mov if len([y for y in gp[k] if y < x]) > 1]:
            continue                             # nor the nearest gap on its left
        if n > 1 and len({i > k for i, x, k in mov}) < 2:
            continue                             # some goods climb, some are lifted down
        fst, seen = [], set()
        for i, x, k in st:                       # the movers are not simply the first n strays
            if len(fst) < n and k not in seen and " " in G[k]:
                seen.add(k)
                fst.append((i, x, k))
        if n and fst == mov:
            continue
        if any(sorted([G[i].count(y) for y in set(G[i]) - {" ", LT[i]}] + [0])[-1]
               > G[i].count(LT[i]) - 2 for i in range(4)):
            continue                             # the shelf's own letter wins by 2 or more
        e = "=" * (2 * W - 9)                    # the shop front, the same in every clue
        out = ["     +" + e + " THE CORNER SHOP " + e + "+"]
        bar = "     +" + "-" * (4 * W - 1) + "+"
        for i in range(4):                       # JAM  |jam jam ___ egg jam ...|
            out.append(NM[LT[i]].upper() + "  |" + " ".join(NM[y] for y in G[i]) + "|")
            out.append(bar)
        return "\n".join(out) + "\n" + str(n) + " home"
    return FB
solve:
def solve(clue):
    P = clue.split("\n")
    T = P.pop()                                   # the "<n> home" caption, copied through
    Q = P[1::2]                                   # the four labelled shelf rows
    L = [x[:3].lower() for x in Q]                # what each shelf is for, as it is written
    H = [x[0] for x in L]
    D = dict(zip(H, L))
    D["_"] = "___"                                # an empty slot on the shelf
    R = [x[6::4] for x in Q]                      # one letter per slot
    G = [list(x) for x in R]
    M = []
    for i, x in enumerate(R):
        for j, y in enumerate(x):
            if y != "_" and y != H[i]:            # a good on somebody else's shelf
                k = H.index(y)
                if R[k][j] == H[i] and "_" in R[k]:   # in line with one of its own shelf's goods
                    M.append((i, j, k))               # standing here, and there is room at home
    for i, j, k in M:
        G[i][j] = "_"                             # it leaves the slot it was standing in
    for i, j, k in M:
        G[k][R[k].index("_")] = H[k]              # and goes into the first gap on its own shelf
    P[1::2] = [q[:6] + " ".join(D[t] for t in g) + "|" for q, g in zip(Q, G)]
    return "\n".join(P) + "\n" + T
